# Thingsboard: current unsafe-reflection omission

8 November 2026. Runtime `334234c24e9008f4a2614b8213b8b2e73b6ba9e1`.
Latest reached: **run-2, TIMEOUT**. Latest accepted forward report: **run-1**.
This accepted report has 13 of the 14 fixed f945 identities, with no additions.
The absent identity is:

```text
java.security.unsafe-reflection
QqsVp4+sxVrhcl8zO3TCQnLuKU/flyz9avYbI4/f3YY=
org.thingsboard.server.common.data.util.ReflectionUtils#getAnnotationProperty
    (java.lang.String, java.lang.String, java.lang.String)
ReflectionUtils.java:27: Class.forName(targetType)
```

It was already absent in the saved campaigns. The current run does not establish
a new regression, but the strict omission remains unresolved. Timeout explains
why no later forward result exists; it does not prove eventual recovery.

## Source and legacy path

The f945 result has two source-to-sink traces, with 27 and 21 locations. Both
start at the Spring request-body parameter `ruleChainMetaData`. The shorter route
is:

```java
// RuleChainController.saveRuleChainMetaData:
// Spring entry rule marks request-body ruleChainMetaData as UNTRUSTED.
return tbRuleChainService.saveRuleChainMetaData(..., ruleChainMetaData, ...);

// DefaultTbRuleChainService delegates to BaseRuleChainService.
// BaseRuleChainService.saveRuleChainMetaData:
List<RuleNode> nodes = ruleChainMetaData.getNodes();
for (RuleNode node : nodes) {
    setSingletonMode(node);
    // ...
}

// BaseRuleChainService.setSingletonMode:
ReflectionUtils.getAnnotationProperty(ruleNode.getType(),
    "org.thingsboard.rule.engine.api.RuleNode", "clusteringMode");

// ReflectionUtils.getAnnotationProperty:
Class<Annotation> annotationClass = (Class<Annotation>) Class.forName(annotationType);
Annotation annotation = Class.forName(targetType).getAnnotation(annotationClass);
return (T) annotationClass.getDeclaredMethod(property).invoke(annotation);
```

The second route puts nodes through `toAddOrUpdate`, `updateRuleNodeConfiguration`
and `RuleChainDataValidator.validateRuleNode` before the same `ruleNode.getType()`
and reflection call. The source `RuleNode.type` is a mutable request-supplied
string, not the constant annotation class name. The first `forName(annotationType)`
is a different call, at JIR instruction 0. The missing sink is
`forName(targetType)`, at instruction 1. Thus dropping constant-base facts does
not explain away the required dynamic path.

The production rule is the `unsafe-reflection` join in
`rules/ruleset/java/security/external-configuration-control.yaml:230`: join
`untrusted-data-source.$UNTRUSTED` to `unsafe-reflection-sink.$UNTRUSTED`.
The library sink rule matches `java.lang.Class.forName($UNTRUSTED,...)`.
The Spring source rule accepts the controller's request parameter.

The JSON receipt preserves both ordered f945 traces, current source excerpts
and hashes. All seven inspected Java source snapshots match the 3 November audit.
All three relevant YAML files match the historically audited f945 bytes. The
current serialized model hash also matches that audit:
`1246cb43621245e0ef971a51052b54a56abd60725860f44824f00f34d57b58f3`.
These pins exclude a changed input at those locations; they do not prove that
current rule specialization or execution matches the old engine.

## Current evidence of reachability

The current log registers the reflection library rule and generates 18 rules
for the unsafe-reflection join. Its mark dictionary includes full mark 205:

```text
java/security/external-configuration-control.yaml:unsafe-reflection#source#1;0;$UNTRUSTED;2
```

The exact run-1 frontier at `analyzer.log:4490` contains these default-context
methods in its analysed set and demand map:

| Method | Outgoing demand rows |
| --- | ---: |
| `ReflectionUtils.getAnnotationProperty` | 1 |
| `RuleChainDataValidator.validateRuleNode` | 37 |
| `BaseRuleChainService.setSingletonMode` | 21 |
| `RuleChainController.saveRuleChainMetaData` | 521 |

These counts match the earlier saved audit's sink/validator/helper pattern.
They prove method-level analysis and remaining guidance, not a concrete T/NORMAL
arrival at instruction 1, the contents of that single row, or evaluation of the
sink predicate with the needed source origin. ZERO-only work can also instantiate
a method. The current log has no instruction-level trace of this flow.

The field route includes `nodes`, a collection element and `type`, but source
expansion, MUST/ANY/STAR facts and call summaries affect its representation. The
source text does not establish a minimum required iteration or field limit.

## What remains unproved

The current evidence does not locate the first lost fact. In particular it does
not distinguish a denied mark request, a loop/block routing problem, loss of a
Target/source permission, or refinement left unfinished by timeout. No focused
current Reflection test or extra real-project run was performed. A later native
trace would need the actual Spring entry-source output and the unsafe-reflection
mark's original/path/tail/layer at each listed call, loop boundary, getter and
ReflectionUtils instruction 1. It must preserve the real rules and source model.

The strict missing identity is retained in the final quality result. It is not
waived as a constant-only case, a proved false positive, or an inevitable later
recovery. Portable evidence: `thingsboard-reflection-current-source-audit.json`.

# Thingsboard run-1: joined static writer binding

8 November 2026. Source runtime `334234c24e9008f4a2614b8213b8b2e73b6ba9e1`.
Latest Thingsboard reached: **run-2, TIMEOUT**. Latest engine-complete run and
accepted forward report: **run-1**. This is a source and bounded-log investigation,
not a new implementation or selected semantics change. Stirling is still active.
No build, new run, JFR, heap, or SARIF analysis was performed for this note.

## 1. The measured work is an extra run-1 guidance phase

`projects/thingsboard/bidi/analyzer.log:4298,4301` records:

| Quantity | Native count/time | Meaning |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| run-1 engine | 521.168831016 s | Excludes joined static binding |
| joined static binding | 292.710897445 s | Includes collection/prune, binding and freeze |
| writer work inside that phase | 284.234864562 s | The work-queue completion below |
| observed candidate memberships | 2,762,679 | Pre-prune raw write/candidate IDs across owners |
| lost memberships | 488,233 | No exactly equal final survivor; not necessarily a definite cleaner kill |
| writer offers | 31,622,618 | Includes repeated offers before owner/ID admission |
| admitted / processed writers | 2,969,858 / 2,969,858 | Fresh `(OwnedScope, raw writer ID)` work |
| candidate inputs | 462,365,666 | Borrow callbacks passing the runtime-domain check |
| duplicate inputs | 0 | Duplicate full input-link key plus group, within one processed writer |
| matched inputs | 33,190,272 | Passed source-authority and full AP selection |
| bound outputs | 33,099,986 | Scalar outputs before builder/parent-writer duplicate admission |

Only 7.178% of counted candidates reach the `matchedInputs` increment;
429,175,394 do not. The source counter does not partition those failures into
ZERO authority, type/mark, geometry, tail or exclusion causes. Zero duplicate
inputs does **not** mean that premise selection is never repeated, or that two
different call sites cannot have the same binding effect.

The writer phase is additional to the 521.169 s engine. The driver subtracts
joined binding time when it reports engine time (`IterationDriver.kt:92`).
Removing this phase's cost alone cannot meet the user's 60-second engine target.

Source paths below are relative to
`core/opentaint-dataflow-core/opentaint-dataflow/src/main/kotlin/org/opentaint/dataflow/bidi/`.

## 2. A joined writer is not a static-pool write point

There are two different mechanisms:

| Mechanism | Purpose | Output/effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Executed local static write | Make the actual concrete mark globally visible now; register a FLOW write for future requests | Static pool supply and write-point state |
| Joined writer binding | Complete caller/block-owned demand guidance after all live work joins, including writes missing at the final normal exit | Thin, immutable guidance rows only |

The first mechanism implements the selected rule that supply occurs at the write
point. `Run1PointResume.localWrite` immediately adds each actual concrete output
to `staticBatch.supplies` (`Run1PointResume.kt:177-200`). `emitOperationResult`
invokes it before later exit handling (`BlockRunState.kt:366-386`). Summary
promotion can publish a computed supply but registers no new write point
(`Run1PointResume.kt:204-243`).

The joined mechanism neither supplies the pool nor invokes the writer request
protocol. It borrows stopped input directories, applies only ordinary AP relation
binding, adds guidance, and recursively binds the newly caller-owned writer.
It executes no configured call suffix, aliases, rule, source hit, live request or
summary publication (`OwnedJoinedStaticWriterBinding.kt:36-39,97-125`). The two
mechanisms are orthogonal under the current contract.

For comparison, the same native log's pool-service statistics have 1,117 writer
rows and 384 FLOW-writer rows (`analyzer.log:4299`). Those pool rows cannot be
equated to 2,969,858 joined writer tasks. The latter include formal/output mark
pairs and recursively rebound owners; they are not that many program assignments.

## 3. Exact writer and input identities

### Writer key

`StaticWriteKey` is `(original InitialAp, raw static result Pattern)`
(`store/KilledStaticWriteStore.kt:10-69`). It retains the complete original base,
path, tail, mark and legal E, plus static output base/path/tail/mark/E and raw FLOW
mx. Concrete input/output marks are packed as one pair; geometry is shared.
The output support layer is not a key coordinate here: the joined binder rebuilds
it as DEMAND. This guidance key is also not an owned protected edge: `Pattern`
has no H coordinate. Do not confuse that baseline guide representation with the
new independent U/H memberships in executable edge stores.

The queue identity adds `(MethodKey, BlockScope/entry port)` through `OwnedScope`.
`offer` admits an ID once in that owner, then queues it. Static originals bypass
this queue and enter the static bridge graph instead
(`OwnedJoinedStaticWriterBinding.kt:49-69`).

The initial inventory is broader than killed-only writes. It observes reached
pre-exit statics, executed intermediate writes and pre-filter results; at joined
quiescence it records exact equality against final admitted/private survivors
(`KilledStaticWriteStore.kt:95-156`; `BlockRunState.kt:795-824`).
`JoinedStaticGuidance.kt:97-129` seeds lost rows, binds every observed nonstatic
writer, and also offers nonstatic/static outgoing DEMAND rows. Newly bound
nonstatic/ZERO originals can add further queued writers.

### Borrowed input key and directories

`OwnedWriterInput` carries the parent owner, complete parent original, actual
Facts, link key and `zeroOnly`. The link key is a `LocalLink`, or a complete
physical `CallerRef` plus `zeroOnly` (`OwnedJoinedStaticWriterBinding.kt:10-33`).
`LocalLink` includes parent scope, point/port, original, layer and child scope
(`BlockSummaryLinks.kt:34-41`). `CallerRef` retains the physical caller, original,
call instruction, stage, caller layer and scope. The within-writer dedup key adds
the actual packet's `GroupKey`, including type, layer, base, E, mx, tail and H
class (`ap/Conclusions.kt:69-93`). Distinct path/mark contents can share a group;
the directory supplies the merged current packet for that exact input group.

After join, `JoinedBindingLease` moves existing directories. It creates no second
standing caller-input store. Runners/actors can then release their other state
before binding (`RunManager.kt:219-246`; `JoinedBindingLease.kt:25-68`).

The two candidate selectors differ substantially:

| Writer owner | Borrow behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Root/method scope | Use the existing callee path index: input positions which are prefixes or extensions of the writer premise; add genuine ZERO-only controls for ZERO writers (`CalleeSubscriptions.kt:108-126`) |
| Internal block scope | Visit **every input group in that child scope**, then let the AP predicate reject it (`JoinedLocalInputs.kt:84-86`; `JoinedStaticGuidance.kt:54-60`) |

The latter is deliberate current source behavior: `BlockSummaryLinks.detachJoinedInputs`
calls `releaseCandidateIndex` before moving the directory
(`BlockSummaryLinks.kt:279-284`). The live block index and conservative transpose
selector exist (`JoinedLocalInputs.kt:36-70`), but are no longer available to the
joined scan. Current counters do not split local versus physical candidate visits.
Therefore the 462 million visits cannot all be attributed to the local scan.

## 4. Why a pool supply cannot replace caller-owned guidance

The baseline specification explicitly requires BIND-W before static composition:
`spec/restricted-demand-static-closure.md`, section 6.2 and section 7. A raw formal
writer cannot be inherited by a caller as if its formal parameter were a caller
register. Use only existing reached inputs. A ZERO writer requires an actual
ZERO-origin Reach control, not an arbitrary reached packet under another original.

```java
void main() {
    Node x = sourceT();
    set(x);
    consume();
}
void set(Node p) {
    C.f = p;
    // An exit cleaner can remove this result from the final summary.
}
void consume() { sinkT(C.f); }
```

```text
At the executed write in set:
  p/T -> S.C.f/T
  -> supply T immediately, as selected
  -> retain the raw writer/candidate independently of the exit summary

Existing main -> set input:
  parent original ZERO; actual p/T

Joined binding:
  bind set's p/T -> S.C.f/T through that actual input
  -> main has ZERO -> S.C.f/T as DEMAND guidance

Static guidance can then connect that writer with the C.f/T -> Target reader.
```

The global fact “T was written to C.f” does not encode the main/caller original
or the route to its source. Nor does it justify making every caller satisfy p/T.
The current binder preserves that route even if exit rules or final canonical
storage erase the executable writer row. It does not re-evaluate a source guard
or introduce `GroundingSupport`; it uses the already executed primitive relation
and existing actual input, with the selected run-1 DEMAND approximation.
The baseline requires processing observed/post-exit primitive writers and their
caller-bound descendants, not arbitrary static-composed closure outputs. Deleting
this phase, binding through the call graph alone, or binding only exact final
survivors would need a new coverage proof; pool availability is not that proof.

## 5. Exact work loop and counter locations

`OwnedJoinedStaticWriterBinding.kt:72-130` does the following for each fresh writer:

```text
rebuild one scalar DEMAND static conclusion
borrow candidate inputs for the complete owner and writer premise
for each runtime-valid input:
    candidateInputs++
    if (input-link key, actual group) was visited for this writer:
        duplicateInputs++; continue
    enforce genuine ZERO/source authority
    matched = satisfying(actual, writer.original, CURRENT)
    if no match: continue
    matchedInputs++
    applySummary(matched, writer.original, raw writer output,
                 original=the complete parent original)
    run1Cover -> global limit -> run1Cover
    for each output scalar:
        boundOutputs++
        seed(parent owner, parent original, static output)
        if parent original is nonstatic: offer(parent owner, raw bound writer ID)
```

`writerOffers` increments before the fresh owner/ID test. `boundOutputs` increments
before builder dedup and before the derived-writer admission test. Thus 33.1 million
outputs are not 33.1 million distinct final guidance rows. Similarly, candidate
keys can be distinct yet repeatedly produce the same parent-owned guide. The
31.6 million offers/admitted-writer ratio is about 10.65, but that is not a direct
speedup bound: the initial inventory, static-original outputs and output fan-out
have different paths through those counters.

## 6. Actual bounded shape examples, with a scope limit

`thingsboard-joined-writer-source-rows.json` preserves three exact body samples,
their log line numbers and decoded field/mark names. All are **fresh post-statement
packets**, not joined binder pair traces (`BodyWorkStatistics.kt:29-30`). In
`MqttTransportHandler.processDevicePublish`, point 186:

```text
this.STAR / XSS-source-UNTRUSTED
  -> S.__spring_registry__.TbClusterService.ANY / generated-XSS-sink_61, D, H=true

this.STAR / generated-XSS-sink_2
  -> S.__spring_registry__.EdgeService.ANY / generated-XSS-sink_2, D, H=true

this.STAR / generated-XSS-sink_73
  -> S.__spring_registry__.TbCoreDeviceRpcService.ANY / generated-XSS-sink_73, D, H=true
```

Each captured packet has one membership, one protected membership and counted
field depth 1. Class `__spring_registry__` is the zero-count anchor; the service
field consumes the field budget. The full generated names and IDs are in the JSON.
These examples prove that short static ANY/DEMAND generated-mark relations exist
under nonstatic premises. They do **not** prove the fraction of all statics, that
these exact rows dominate joined binding, or which actual input pairs produced
its 462 million candidate visits. No joined row/input sampling is enabled in the
current source/log, so that link remains unmeasured.

## 7. Candidate pair-elimination directions for a future proposal

These are proof/measurement targets, not selected code changes. The earlier
unselected proposal `docs/design/bidirectional-joined-writer-observer-work-next-iteration-20261104.md`
already describes exact premise-selection sharing; it is still absent here.

### A. Select once per complete owner/premise, not once per static output

Neither root nor local selection depends on the writer's result. Neither does
`satisfying(actual, writer.original)`. With fixed joined inputs, group rows by
complete `(OwnedScope, InitialAp, mode)` and obtain their ordered matches once.
Apply all raw output columns with their own unchanged mx/geometry afterward.
This avoids entire repeated candidate scans/matches for wide output families.
It is stronger than making an individual hash operation faster. Measure columns
per exact premise, local/root selection counts and reusable matched-input width
before choosing a scratch plan or changing traversal order.

### B. Restore sparse local candidate selection, and measure mark/type sparsity

The live local index is already a conservative transpose of the ordinary matcher.
A future joined lease could retain or rebuild that capability rather than scan
all local groups per writer. A mark/type-aware selector could additionally reject
whole candidate sets which cannot contain the writer's selected full mark. The
current physical index is path-only; `satisfyingPart` rejects a concrete premise
on FLOW input and filters Taint leaves by the exact mark afterward
(`ap/Summary.kt:53-60,79-83`).

Prove that the sparse candidate sequence is a superset of native successful
matches, preserve native order where required, then retain the unchanged full
matcher. Measure failure reasons first: the aggregate 92.82% unmatched rate does
not reveal how much is wrong marks versus unrelated local bases versus tails/E.
Keeping an index longer also has a memory cost; this note does not select one.

### C. For fixed concrete ANY output, bind support once per parent original

A more specific algorithmic opportunity is a writer with a concrete STAR premise
and a concrete ANY result, in FULL mode:

```text
I = p.STAR/T; output = S.C.f.ANY/U; empty legal initial E
existing inputs from two physical call sites:
  parent original q.STAR/T; actual p.a.ANY/T
  parent original q.STAR/T; actual p.b.ANY/T

native output of both bindings:
  q.STAR/T -> S.C.f.ANY/U, DEMAND
```

The result ANY discards the actual suffix (`ap/Reference.kt:286,308-310`), its
concrete U is fixed, and joined output is DEMAND. Call position is not exported
by `onBound`, which receives only parent owner, complete original and Pattern.
Thus, for this proved cell, a support set keyed by complete parent owner/original
can potentially replace many per-call-site applications with one guide output.
The native ZERO authority and matching-existence proof still precede that step.
The current duplicate-input key deliberately distinguishes the two call sites,
so its zero duplicate count cannot estimate this opportunity.

This candidate needs a concrete native lemma covering the full AP operation,
global limit, run1Cover and guide representation, plus dynamic parent-queue
equivalence. It does not allow merging actual executable inputs or ND bindings.
It is not valid without further proof for STAR outputs (suffix correlation
survives), FLOW output mx/mark-dependent results, other marks, source authority,
or a packet with multiple outputs. Keep exact facts/H for any native computation;
the observation that the existing thin guide drops H is not permission to change
executable edge protection. Measure distinct parent-original supports and final
new guide outputs before claiming a factor reduction.

The shared requirement is to eliminate provably redundant **writer/input pairs**,
not merely accelerate their construction. Every retained original-to-static
guidance route must remain; a reached pool group alone cannot replace that route.

## 8. The current lazy closure still has an eager writer-binding prefix

There is a genuine distinction between two stages:

```text
Phase A now: all primitive/observed W + reached input links
             -> eagerly compute caller-/parent-bound W and B seeds
Phase B now: freeze W/R/Target attachments and the shared B graph
             -> lazily compose only paths needed by run-2 C2/C5 queries
```

Phase A is **not limited to the 488,233 lost candidate memberships**. Lost IDs
are seeded directly (`JoinedStaticGuidance.kt:97-101`), but every observed
nonstatic writer is offered for binding (`104-106`), as are nonstatic/static
DEMAND exit rows (`122-129`). The fixed point binds all fresh queued writers
against their existing input candidates. There is no reader-demand or pool-
already-reached test in that work loop. Final prune uses exact guidance-key
equality against final retained summaries/private B, not semantic region coverage
(`KilledStaticWriteStore.kt:129-151`). A key absent by that exact equality is
conservatively lost; a partial, changed or canonicalized survivor can leave it.

Thus a future design could consider a **symbolic Phase A**, not only optimize
Phase B composition: freeze primitive writers, exact input-binding relations,
owners and ports; derive bound attachments only when a run-2 query asks for
them. This could avoid bindings whose results no query ever needs. It is a new
lazy graph/capability design with additional proof and memory obligations, not
an implementation detail justified by pool reachability.

Required query coverage includes at least:

- **C2 direct/local/inherited entry selection.** `StaticEntryLookup.kt:19-47`
  reads entries and marked predecessor witnesses. Lazy binding must expose every
  relevant marked writer, including raw killed writes, before returning an empty
  result or declaring the complete command family covered.
- **C5 paired origin/output paths.** `StaticPairLookup.kt:44-82` walks mapped
  paths and offers their complete demand pair. Distinct nonstatic/ZERO originals
  are not interchangeable; an equal global C.f/T does not cover them. The marked
  predecessor and every output budget remain paired, including nested block
  scope/port and recursive parent routes.
- **Target control and genuine ZERO origins.** `StaticPairLookup.kt:11-41`
  follows terminal-reader inputs through incoming writers/bridges. It must still
  derive `ZERO -> DemandTarget` guidance when a real ZERO-origin source reaches
  the static read, including killed-at-exit writes. The typed static-shortcut
  Target probe explicitly requires a complete W/B path with a genuine ZERO
  origin (`DemandStore.kt:302-337`). A pool group or unrelated reached ZERO cannot
  substitute for that path.
- **Static originals produced by binding.** Such a result becomes a B bridge,
  which can be inherited through the call graph and used to reach a later R or
  Target. A lazy producer cannot stop merely because the immediate output is
  already marked or because its direct local consumer set is empty.

The current lease closes at the end of joined preparation
(`RunManager.kt:253-264`). A symbolic design must therefore keep a compact,
independently owned immutable representation of the necessary binding inputs,
or prove a smaller equivalent support relation. It cannot capture actors,
subscriber ports, live packet directories, or assume those inputs remain
available after release. Retaining the whole raw lease into run-2 would undo
the selected release/memory contract and needs separate measurement.

Its proof target is equality to the current finite BIND-W fixed point followed
by the existing lazy static-path view, for each complete C2/C5/Target query.
Recursive callers and nested loops need query-state dedup and negative-query
completeness. Existing query-local coverage may stop a search only after all
commands or paired outputs needed for that query are proved covered. This note
does not supply that proof or select the redesign. Factor-by-complete-premise
and sparse ephemeral candidate selection remain the cleaner exact first scope.

# Current native receiver-reset result

8 November 2026. Isolated detached validation checkout at
`334234c24e9008f4a2614b8213b8b2e73b6ba9e1`. The production checkout, runtime
distribution and campaign outputs were not changed.

The exact historical `UnresolvedReceiverSourceResetTest` source compiled with
no adapter. SHA-256:
`5c1be7a849aa7776cfc0641dc7a58d3096f6983c4205414e80fb21d4f68162fc`.
The strict native outcome is **2 tests, 1 failure, 0 errors**:

| Native case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `command.add(sourceT()); sinkA(command)` | Reports the required sink; control passes |
| `command.add(sourceT()); command.add("literal"); sinkA(command)` | No report; required-finding assertion fails |

Both complete FULL **run-1** with `NO_DEMAND_EDGE`. The 0.208-second native test
suite is a small completed witness, not an analyzer timeout. Gradle spent 1m 28s
building the isolated checkout and returned exit 1 because the strict retention
assertion failed. It used `--max-workers=2`.

The trace has ZERO-origin NORMAL exact data T, then a ZERO-origin NORMAL exact
receiver A. With the literal call, A is present at the literal instruction input
and absent at the sink input. The direct-use control carries A to the sink.
The source topology binds the receiver to This, passes it through unresolved
identity, executes the exact return reset, then binds back. The literal argument
cannot satisfy the source's `CM(arg0,T)` guard, so no replacement A is generated.

This confirms the previously identified loss in the **current reduced native
call-plan fixture**. It injects no demands, saved summaries, predefined summaries
or findings. It does not prove that this is the first actual loss in the current
Stirling project. The earlier real-JIR audit found the same add-55/add-56 source
and reset topology; the six audited production lowering/rule files remain byte
identical. Actual current project T/A arrivals at those calls were not traced.

No semantics fix was selected or applied. The failing required-finding assertion
is preserved, and none of the three strict historical Stirling omissions is
waived. `command.txt`, `gradle.log`, `native-tests.xml`, `native-trace.txt` and
`execution.json` retain the command, exact outcomes and source pins. The
validation checkout has no tracked diff; its only added test is the preserved
fixture. The campaign core's passing suite and this additional intentionally
strict failing coverage witness are separate results.

package org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi

import org.opentaint.dataflow.ap.ifds.AccessPathBase
import org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.ap.*
import org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.driver.FixedLimits
import org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.engine.*
import org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.fixtures.DriverFixtures
import org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.interp.*
import org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.interp.CallPoint.*
import org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.interp.StageKind.*
import kotlin.test.*
import kotlin.time.Duration.Companion.seconds

/** EXTERNAL UNRUN diagnostic. This is the candidate JIR call-plan shape, not a
 * claim that the real Stirling literal call has already been traced. The actual
 * provider's source/reset metadata and unresolved resolution must be checked.
 *
 * Code: List c=new ArrayList(); c.add(source()); [c.add("literal");] sink(c);
 * Rule: CM(arg0, UNTRUSTED) assigns ARGS to this; sink checks ARGS on arg0.
 * Metadata: source reset set contains ARGS at this. As in JIRCallPlanBuilder,
 * SOURCES bypasses return cleanup; ordinary unresolved This is cleaned before
 * bind-back. Unlike a fabricated predefined summary, both add calls execute all
 * these stages and only the first add has an actual marked argument.
 */
class UnresolvedReceiverSourceResetTest {
    private fun check(withLiteral: Boolean) {
        DriverFixtures().use { f ->
            val p=f.program
            val root=p.method("unresolved source receiver withLiteral=$withLiteral",
                listOf(listOf(1),listOf(2),listOf(3),listOf(4),emptyList()),4).key()
            val command=AccessPathBase.LocalVar(0)
            val data=AccessPathBase.LocalVar(1)
            val receiver=AccessPathBase.This
            val arg=AccessPathBase.Argument(0)
            val untrusted=MarkSlot.Concrete(p.mark("T"))
            val args=MarkSlot.Concrete(p.mark("U"))
            val owner=FormOwner()
            fun id(at:Int,kind:RuleKind)=RuleOccurrenceId(FormKey(owner,root.method,root,p.inst(root,at)),kind,0)
            val sourceId=id(0,RuleKind.ENTRY_SOURCE)
            val source=PathEdge(ZERO_FACT,p.pattern(data,mark=untrusted).fact,ExclusionSet.Empty)
            p.entry(root,RuleStatement(MicroEdgeBuilder().apply {
                keepZero(); sourceEdge(source,ActionId(sourceId,ActionRole.SOURCE,0))
            }.build(),StatementSummary.EMPTY,emptyList()))
            fun add(at:Int,withData:Boolean) {
                val b=RulePredicate.Builder(f.cancellation,f.manager.marks)
                val sourceId=id(at,RuleKind.CALL_SOURCE)
                val action=SourceAction(ActionId(sourceId,ActionRole.SOURCE,0),p.pattern(receiver,mark=args).fact)
                val rule=SourceRuleOccurrence(sourceId,b.build(b.leaf(p.pattern(arg,mark=untrusted))),listOf(action))
                val bind=mutableListOf(ZERO_KEEP,starEdge(command,emptyList(),receiver,emptyList()))
                if(withData)bind+=starEdge(data,emptyList(),arg,emptyList())
                p.call(root,at,CallPlan(setOf(command,data),listOf(
                    CallStage.Edges(BEFORE,BOUND,BIND_IN,f.summary(*bind.toTypedArray())),
                    CallStage.Edges(BOUND,REWRITTEN,SOURCES,MicroEdgeBuilder().apply { keepZero(); source(rule) }.buildStage()),
                    CallStage.Actions(BOUND,ADDED,emptyList()),
                    CallStage.Edges(ADDED,RETURNED,UNRESOLVED,f.summary(keepEdge(receiver),keepEdge(arg))),
                    CallStage.Edges(ADDED,RETURNED,UNRESOLVED,StatementSummary.EMPTY),
                    CallStage.Actions.run1FullReturnRewriter(listOf(CleanStep.Clean(Cleaner(receiver,null,CleanReach.EXACT,args.mark))),f.manager.marks),
                    CallStage.Edges(REWRITTEN,AFTER,BIND_BACK,f.summary(
                        starEdge(receiver,emptyList(),command,emptyList()),starEdge(arg,emptyList(),data,emptyList()))),
                ),emptyList(),BEFORE,AFTER))
            }
            add(1,true)
            if(withLiteral)add(2,false) else p.statement(root,2,f.summary(ZERO_KEEP,keepEdge(command),keepEdge(data)))
            val sink=SinkRule(f.rule("receiver ARGS at ProcessBuilder"),0,listOf(p.pattern(arg,mark=args)),emptyList())
            p.call(root,3,CallPlan(setOf(command),listOf(
                CallStage.Edges(BEFORE,BOUND,BIND_IN,f.summary(ZERO_KEEP,starEdge(command,emptyList(),arg,emptyList()))),
                CallStage.Actions(BOUND,ADDED,emptyList()),
                CallStage.Edges(ADDED,RETURNED,UNRESOLVED,f.summary(keepEdge(arg))),
                CallStage.Actions(RETURNED,REWRITTEN,emptyList()),
                CallStage.Edges(REWRITTEN,AFTER,BIND_BACK,f.summary(starEdge(arg,emptyList(),command,emptyList()))),
            ),listOf(sink),BEFORE,AFTER))
            val driver=f.driver(FixedLimits(listOf(1,1,2,3)),20.seconds,run1MarkMode=MarkMode.FULL)
            val report=driver.analyze(listOf(root))
            val rows=f.processed.filter { it.run==1 && it.method==root }.map { row ->
                "at=${row.delta.node.location.index} original=${row.delta.premise.members.map { it.toPattern() }} result=${f.ops.leaves(row.delta.facts).toList()} layer=${row.delta.facts.layer}"
            }
            println("UNRESOLVED_RECEIVER_RESET literal=$withLiteral end=${report.end} reports=${report.entries.map { it.descriptor.key }}")
            rows.forEach(::println)
            assertEquals(RunStatus.COMPLETE,report.end.status)
            assertEquals(listOf(sink.rule.id),report.entries.map { it.descriptor.key.ruleId },"Lost sticky list receiver label after a nonmatching add; inspect printed native rows")
        }
    }
    @Test fun `marked add directly followed by constructor sink`()=check(false)
    @Test fun `marked add followed by literal add retains receiver label`()=check(true)
}
